references.text: The Lord was with Joseph and gave him success in everything he did. His master's recognition of the Lord's blessing over Joseph laid the foundation for the trust and favor Joseph gained.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, who had charge of all that he owned – a strong parallel to how Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his whole household and gave him everything he owned into his hand.
A parallel pattern is seen when the prison warden puts Joseph over all the prisoners and gives him responsibility, using the same language about the Lord being with him and giving him success.
In Stephen's speech, it is referred that God was with Joseph and rescued him from all his troubles, and gave him favor and wisdom – a summary of Joseph's journey from slave to trusted servant.

The expression 'to find favor in someone's eyes' (מצא חן בעיני) is used repeatedly in the patriarchal narratives, referring to grace and goodwill from a superior – the same expression used about Joseph and Potiphar.
Both verses illustrate the same theological principle: God's presence ensures that Joseph finds favor with superiors in times of crisis.
This verse is a theological summary linking Joseph's time with Potiphar (39:4) directly to his final exaltation under Pharaoh.
